root_idea.summary: The root centers on something issuing or being generated from something else, especially a copious flow, and also on motion or commotion.
root_idea.development: The primary development runs from milk flowing abundantly to rain, tribute, provision, bounty, and brisk trade; a second branch concerns movement, vigorous running, quivering, and the gleaming or pearl-like appearance of things.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Quranic adjective citation form.
Displayed as the normalized lexical form مِدْرَارٌ.

senses.definition: Brilliant, shining, or gleaming like a pearl; in the Quranic expression, a star of striking brightness and clarity.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of the star in the parable of the light; the pearl comparison highlights whiteness, clearness, and beauty.

senses.definition: Pouring down abundantly; abundant and copious, especially of rain sent forth from the sky.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic usage applies the milk-flow image to rain and describes rain as copious or abundant; it occurs in descriptions of divine provision and punishment or blessing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flow or become copious, especially of milk; by extension, to flow abundantly of tears, sweat, water, and similar fluids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic verb is used of fluids and of their becoming plentiful or streaming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be consecutive or continue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived extension describing an event or thing as continuing without interruption.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run vehemently, or to run easily and without interruption.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse or similar riding animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become tangled or luxuriant through abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To yield or emit milk copiously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a she-camel, ewe, she-goat, or udder in a milk-yielding construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour in abundantly, especially of tribute or tax revenue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical extension of abundant milk-flow to revenue collected for a community.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour down rain abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the sky in a rain-pouring construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce or give forth what one has; to be bountiful, or to become commercially productive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's resources, the world as bountiful, or a market whose goods sell briskly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of ducts or veins, to become filled with milk or blood; of a vein, to pulsate continuously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bodily-fluid and pulsation uses are conventional extensions of flowing and continuous movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an arrow, to turn smoothly and audibly on the nail of the thumb when tested for hardness, straightness, and compactness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical archery expression describing the testing motion of an arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become soft, tender, or supple.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate adjectival or stative use of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a lamp, to give light, shine, or shine brightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a lamp or other source of light.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man's face, to become goodly after illness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized stative use describing recovery of the face's appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause milk to flow or draw it forth; to suck or draw milk, or to milk an animal by stroking its teats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both transitively for causing milk-flow and of an animal or person drawing milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause tribute or tax revenue to come in abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative economic extension of making milk flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause urine to flow plentifully; to act as a diuretic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a medicine or other agent; related medical usage includes promoting menstrual flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ply or press importunately until something is yielded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic causative construction developed from repeatedly eliciting milk-flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw or procure the means of subsistence, or to draw divine favor by gratitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of sustenance and blessing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wind, to draw a shower from clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cloud construction describes bringing forth fine rain; a related usage expresses seeking or expecting rain from clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a vein to flow, fill with blood, or move; more generally, to put something in motion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of anger affecting a vein and of initiating motion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist a spindle vehemently so that its rapid rotation makes it seem still.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of spinning a spindle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an arrow turn smoothly on the nail of the thumb in the technical arrow test.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative counterpart of the specialized Form I archery use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To inflict an uninterrupted beating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of repeated blows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-goat, to desire the ram.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or euphemistic use connecting desire for mating with the subsequent production of milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak or talk much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical extension of continued or abundant outpouring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To chew or mumble an unripe date with toothless gums.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a child or of someone whose speech or chewing resembles that of a toothless child.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lose one's teeth so that their sockets become apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate use describing the condition of the gums after tooth loss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move about or be in commotion; to quiver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing in motion, of a piece of flesh quivering, and idiomatically of a woman's buttocks quivering while she walks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk; by extension, milch animals and the teats of a camel or other cloven-footed animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun is also used substantively for the product and its sources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idioms, a deed, gift, bounty, wealth, or good proceeding from someone; hence an expression of praise or, in negation, of blame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrases لِلّٰهِ دَرُّهُ and لَا دَرَّ دَرُّهُ preserve the original image of abundant milk while expressing admiration, blessing, or censure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The soul or inner self.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical synonym of نَفْسٌ, especially in expressions describing a generous or manly disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pearl, especially a large pearl.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is also used as a collective noun, with recorded plural forms دُرَرٌ and دُرَّاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Copious flowing milk; a flow, stream, or mode of flowing of milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical discussion distinguishes a general abundance of milk from a single flow in some usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pouring forth of clouds or showers; flowing or streaming abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of clouds and rain; the historical Quran comparison in the lexical discussion is not treated as a modern verse citation for this headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Brisk commercial activity, with goods selling much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a market in contrast with slack or stagnant trade.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continuous movement or uninterrupted running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the leg or stride of a horse and of a horse passing without being turned aside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blood, by comparison with milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use, including the blood of warfare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on milk as sustenance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A whip or scourge used for beating or flogging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional noun for an implement of punishment, particularly the whip associated with the Sultan.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The right course or direction of a road; a tract or point directly in front of something; the direction from which wind blows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a road's beaten or elevated track, the area opposite a house, or the wind's point of origin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swift, especially a horse or similar animal that is fast and compactly built.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective can emphasize speed, firmness, or compact construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse or mare, running much or frequently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the horse-related adjective, distinct from the Quranic pearl-like adjective دُرِّيٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chaste or most refined dialect of Persian.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained by reference to دَرّ, a district name or a word meaning “door” or “gate.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The glistening or shining quality of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A poetic relational use associated with the clarity of pearls or likened to the shining star.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spindle used for spinning wool or cotton.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete instrument noun associated with vigorous turning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of the gums where the teeth grow, especially in a child or after the teeth have fallen out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also reported, less commonly, for the tip or root of the tongue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An onomatopoeic sound of water rushing through the beds of valleys.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a sound noun, distinct from the verbal noun of chewing or mumbling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular tree, also called شَجَرَةُ البَقِّ and identified in later usage with the elm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun with a recorded association with gall-like excrescences containing insects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of a drum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate onomatopoeic noun from the botanical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A whirlpool or violently turbulent place in the sea from which a ship scarcely escapes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of dangerous marine turbulence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abounding in milk; a milch she-camel, ewe, she-goat, or udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied to milk-producing animals and their udders.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pouring down abundant rain, said of the sky or a cloud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjective transferring abundant milk-flow to rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continual and uninterrupted sustenance or means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to provision or livelihood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lamp that gives light or shines brightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive or adjectival use describing a luminous lamp.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A copious flowing or streaming of milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for abundant milk-flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medicine that promotes urine flow; by extension, an agent that promotes menstrual flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The medical uses are recorded under specialized collocations for diuresis and emmenagogy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who twists a spindle so vigorously that it seems still from the speed of its rotation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial description of spinning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Arrows whose flight resembles streaming milk because of the force with which they are propelled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative poetic description of a group of arrows in flight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, running far without being turned aside.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative active-participial use describing sustained, unobstructed running.

cautions: The Quranic form دُرِّيٌّ is normalized under the adjective citation form and is kept distinct from the horse adjective دَرِّيٌّ and the sword-related classical use.

A historical Quran citation appearing in the Lane discussion of دِرَّةٌ has not been converted into a modern verse location because the lexical evidence does not independently identify it as a QAC occurrence of that headword.
